messages.subject: [GSOC2015 Looking for mentor]
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I am a student of Math (statistics) in Poland University of Wrocław, I have some experience in R:
* creating scorecards using glm in R
* projects for predicting stock prices and hedging portfolios with american/european/quanto, static hedging, delta hedging, explicit finite difference method using R
* now i'm working on automatic time series forecasting in R

I have also some ideas of new packages (I'm not sure if they exist) (e.g package for life insurance maths or actuacial mathematics - ruin probability and connected topics).If someone is interested in cooperation, please leave the message:)

Thank You for any help!

Best regards!
Kasia Staniewicz

messages.subject: Re: [GSOC2015 Looking for mentor]
messages.body_plain:
Dear Katarzyna,

Many thanks for your interest. What we do every year is to set up a wiki
page where mentors and students can post their proposals and get in
touch. So, please, stay tuned. Meanwhile, feel free to approach any
possible mentor and you can also prepare a proposal.

>
> I have also some ideas of new packages (I'm not sure if they exist)

Then, you can should check on CRAN. In particular, try the appropriate
Task View.

Best wishes,

Virgilio

Best,

Virgilio

messages.subject: mlr - Machine Learning in R
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have added a (not 100% finished project) proposal here:

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2015/wiki/table-of-proposed-coding-projects

It links to here:

https://github.com/berndbischl/mlr/wiki/mlr-GSOC-2015-Proposal

It might change in the next days, as I want more feedback from our complete devel team. I will report here when stuff is officially done.

Also, like the proposal says: If you are interested in a somewhat related topic that still makes sense for mlr, please approach us and / or discuss here.

Bernd

messages.subject: Questions on GSoC'15
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

Two quick questions.

1. Would it be possible to apply both as a mentor and a student? I developed an R package during last year, but I feel like it needs fresh eyes and I think it will make a nice GSoC project. On the other hand, I'm interested in applying again as a student (I participated in 2013's GSoC), but I would choose to be student before applying to be a mentor.

2. As rwiki is down, Where should we look for projects and propose new ones? Should we take this https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2015/wiki as the new official wiki for GSoC?

Best regards,
Xavi.
